title: Why does silence detect find one gap, not five?
fullTitle: FFmpeg silencedetect Finds 1 of 5 Gaps: What n and d Really Do

scenes.narration: You run silence detect with its defaults on a clip with five gaps. It reports one. Is the filter broken? A synthetic tone, five gaps of known length and level, on f f m peg six point one point one.

Gap A is two and a half seconds of digital zero, B half a second. C, D and E are one second of noise, peaking at minus forty nine, fifty four and sixty six d b. Reader one is what f f m peg prints. Reader two is the raw samples.
captions: A, B: digital zero. C, D, E: noise.

scenes.narration: The default d is two seconds, so only gap A counts. With d equals one, A and E. With d equals zero point five, A, B and E: a gap exactly as long as d counts. At zero point five oh oh one, B is gone.
captions: d=0.5 keeps B. d=0.5001 drops it.

scenes.narration: Now n. It is compared with every sample, not an average. At minus sixty d b: A, B, E. At minus fifty, D joins. C stays out: its r m s is minus fifty four, its loudest sample minus forty nine. Only minus forty takes it.
captions: n=-60dB: A, B, E. n=-50dB: A, B, D, E.

scenes.narration: Zero point zero zero one is minus sixty d b, identical output. Minus fifty without d b is refused. n equals zero finds nothing, not even digital zero. On sixteen bit audio, one point five finds nothing: the threshold overflows. On float audio, everything is silent.
captions: n=0.001 is n=-60dB. n=-50 is refused.
n=1.5: 16 bit finds nothing, float finds all.

scenes.narration: Edges are the true ones, to the sample. On sixteen bit audio the level is cut to an integer: thirty one is silent at minus sixty, thirty two is not. Printed times keep six digits. In stereo, both channels must be quiet.
captions: 16 bit level cut to an integer: 31 yes, 32 no.

scenes.narration: Set d to the shortest gap you care about, and n above the peak of the noise, not its average. Not tested: other builds, real recordings, compressed audio.
captions: d = shortest gap. n = above the noise peak.
Not tested: other builds, real recordings.
